before: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain a mystery.
after: Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now all days. Please prepare to be surprised constantly.
after: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.

speaker: (narration)
before: 'Welcome,' says a tiny, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions.'
after: 'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'

speaker: (narration)
before: A curator with a feather duster and a very small smile patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
after: You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. (A battle.)
after: You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will be less themselves. This is a feature.'
after: 'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'

speaker: (narration)
before: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
after: 'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'

speaker: (narration)
before: 'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to His Perfection. Reviewed. Approved.
after: 'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain_title}. Reviewed. Approved.

speaker: (narration)
before: NOTE: it will spread. I cannot say I am sorry about that. I am very busy.'
after: NOTE: it will spread. What grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'

speaker: (narration)
before: Somewhere in the Verdant Dump, if the Dump is free, a flower opens. You go back.
after: You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.

speaker: (narration)
before: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height. It is exhausting. A story event.
after: You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.

speaker: (narration)
before: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for a long time. The lamp has a small, hand-made lampshade. Something about it is very, very human.
after: You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.

speaker: (narration)
before: They are beautiful. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
after: You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.

speaker: (narration)
before: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
after: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.

speaker: (narration)
before: The frame is old gold, worth a good deal. You leave the mirror hanging. It was never about the frame, and you were told as much.
after: You remove the old gold frame. The mirror remains hanging; you can still see yourself. The gold will sell for a good price.

speaker: (narration)
before: They tell you what they smiled at: a funeral, a wedding, a bird. When you rise, you carry something heavy and exact. You are not going to forget what this cost.
after: You listen to what they smiled at: a funeral, a wedding, a bird. When you rise, you repeat their names to yourself.

speaker: (narration)
before: A little brass plate for donations to His Perfection, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.
after: You find the brass collection plate bolted to the wall, marked for {villain_title}. You take the coins.

speaker: (narration)
before: It is, after all, other people's money, and they would want it back.
after: You close your hand around the money and leave the empty plate.

speaker: (narration)
before: At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.
after: You find a pot of coins on the top landing, left as a tip by the last climber. You rub your legs and pocket it.

speaker: (narration)
before: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.
after: You keep reading. Page after page describes work that helped people.

speaker: (narration)
before: Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.
after: You read the last plan twice. You recognise the care in it. You close the journal gently.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.
after: I've walked a long way. Everyone I met was afraid of you.

speaker: Primm
before: Every one of them has a number. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?
after: Every one of them has a number. I can account for every citizen. Nobody need be overlooked.

speaker: Primm
before: This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.
after: Please remain still. I know how to put this right.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Because some things are five. Some people are.
after: People are different. You know that.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: Because some things are five. Some people are.
after: People are different. You know that.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards. You can't copy what I do with them. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards. What I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
after: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: A name is something you sign yourself. Nobody gets to fill it in for you. Not even you.
after: My name is mine to sign. You don't get to decide who I am.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You kept everything. Every face, every rule, every house on that table. But nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
after: You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: You kept everything. Every face, every rule, every house on that table. But nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.
after: You kept every face and every house. Nothing grows if you refuse to let anything go.

speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
before: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch how it's done.
after: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting go. I won't keep living in what you did.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, rolling a very small bandage off a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
after: You see Grandmaster Flex step from behind a pillar, unwinding a bandage from his arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: The Grand Chef, restored, in a clean apron, with a ladle. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course not.'
after: You see the Grand Chef in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? Let me help.'

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: 'It applies to him. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
after: 'The rules must answer for him too.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)

speaker: (narration)
before: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the walls of the castle begin to come down.
after: You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.

speaker: (narration)
before: In the Showcase Quarter a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.
after: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.

speaker: (narration)
before: Fig Sly is already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.
after: You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.
after: You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.

speaker: (narration)
before: Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.
after: You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.

speaker: (narration)
before: Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.
after: You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Pathwork Throne
after: the Pathwork Throne

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.
after: You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.

speaker: (narration)
before: The voice of {villain}: nobody. He never really got to be heard, and that was rather the point.
after: {villain}'s rule is over. The voices of the kingdom remain.

speaker: (narration)
before: In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B
after: For everyone who waited to be heard.

speaker: (narration)
before: No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.
after: For everyone learning to choose again.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
after: Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I am going to cry anyway. In triplicate.
after: I think I am going to cry. I have wanted to for a very long time.

speaker: Primm
before: Everything is possible when it is filed correctly. Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years. I have only been looking after it.
after: Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years. I have only been looking after it. Surely you can see that.

speaker: (narration)
before: Height: average. Distinguishing features: none, we hope. Last seen leaving a Ministry facility, ten years ago, in the company of a traitor.
after: Height: average. Distinguishing features: none, we hope. Last seen leaving a Ministry facility in the company of a traitor.

speaker: (check key)
before: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
after: He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.

speaker: (check key)
before: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, and Pip measured your head without asking. Good. That is Crosspath.
after: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, Pip measured you. That is {town}, dearie. Try leaving with the same hat.

speaker: (check key)
before: Here: a trophy. Everyone gets one. Don't make that face. I didn't make the rule. I did make the trophy.
after: Here: a trophy. Everybody gets one. I made it myself, so participate carefully.

speaker: (check key)
before: Sorted and saved. You are starting to look like someone who means it. Starting.
after: Sorted and saved. Your own deck, at last. Now you may take personal offence when it loses.

speaker: (check key)
before: Well done, dearie. You fight better than you look, and you look half drowned.
after: Well done, dearie. You settled the ghosts. Next, settle yourself somewhere dry.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The key is in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners. This town has a great many odd corners. I am one of them.
after: The key is in a hidden chest in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: The way up Mount Swolympus is open. The trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... it's very... thin.
after: Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... never gets enough credit for being there.

speaker: Basil
before: That's the card! One seat, three courses, survival optional. Oh, I'm so excited I could whisk.
after: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited. I think. It feels a lot like the other thing.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move on its own. I've checked. For some decades.
after: Process two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move itself. I've given it a very fair chance.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Not mine, please. I've grown attached.
after: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Please leave mine; we've been through so much together.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Two scavengers. The paw prints are fresh. So is the smell of stolen compost.
after: Two scavengers in the Dump. Fresh paw prints, freshly stolen compost. A trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Road's clear. For now. Give it ten minutes and it won't be. Chalk's still fresh.
after: Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
before: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day,' he says, between reps. 'In my cave. Show me yours.'
after: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'In my cave. Show me yours. No standing ovation required.'

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
before: He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it with pride. And stretch.'
after: He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it. Stretch. That order.'

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
before: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST,' says His Majesty. 'We... sampled it. We would be glad to explain, after you leave.'
after: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
before: 'The compost was for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. Checkmate.'
after: 'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'

speaker: The Rescuer
before: 'You came back,' they say. 'I told them you would not. I told them nobody could be that stubborn.'
after: 'You came back,' they say. 'I hoped you would. I told them you would not.'

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
before: 'Subject 1! You came back to us. And you've grown. Remarkable. The draining has been very good for your posture.'
after: 'Subject 1. You came back to us. You have grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles. I must examine the records.'

speaker: Sable
before: This one's a misprint, darling. Two typos. More character than most knights.
after: Two typos, darling. One misprint. Such a small card, such a complicated past.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: That one's for emergencies! Or Tuesdays! Today's both!
after: Emergency tonic! Works on Tuesdays too! That's when I test the emergency tonic!

speaker: Pip Threadwell
before: Hat! You need a hat! Your head is a tragedy waiting for a brim!
after: Hat! Your next adventure needs a dramatic opening! Preferably above the eyebrows!

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Shh. Listen. ...That crinkle? Foil.
after: Shh. That crinkle? Foil. Please let it finish.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Free a road and its pack comes in. I'll be right here. Sniffing. Respectfully.
after: Free a road and its pack comes in. I'll be here, providing shelf esteem.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Hydration is mandatory. So is stretching. I'm still bad at the stretching.
after: Hydration. Stretching. Sorry, am I ordering again? I meant we could do them together.

speaker: Chet Thunderabs
before: Operators are standing by! The operator is me! I'm standing! By!
after: Operators are standing by! It's me! I tried sitting! LOST THE ENERGY!

speaker: Kyle
before: brb, haunting. jk. unless?
after: brb, haunting. actually stay. nobody reads the 'be right back' part.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: The cake is decorative, darling. So am I. Neither of us is for eating.
after: Decorative cake, darling. Please admire it without cutlery.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: I have tasted my chalk again. Notes of limestone. A disappointing vintage.
after: Chalk again. Notes of limestone. Excellent body, no business being in my mouth.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Savannah Souffle calls that plating? A crime. A beautiful, beautiful crime.
after: Savannah Souffle calls that plating? WHOOSH! That's the sound of me declining to comment!

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: The dishwasher talks back. I have learned so much. Mostly about rinsing.
after: The dishwasher talks back. I listen. Wisdom sometimes arrives with a rinse cycle.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Three years in the parlour, and he hasn't complained once. That's him all over.
after: He has been in the parlour three years. I still tell him when someone comes to the door.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: 27-B needs a 27-C. 27-C needs a 27-B. I've taken up knitting.
after: 27-B needs 27-C. 27-C needs 27-B. I keep both forms beside his chair.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: About the barn... and the goat. We will let that one compost quietly.
after: About the barn... I will help mend it. The goat may prefer that I begin elsewhere.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Eight years of saving it up.
after: Dad says hi. We have so much to tell each other. Sometimes we just sit together.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: Eight years up that road. The walk home was shorter. Funny, that.
after: Eight years up that road. I knew every turn on the way home. Dad was still at the gate.

speaker: Brindle the Baker
before: Fresh bread! Fresh-ish bread! Flour in my whiskers again: free seasoning!
after: Fresh bread! Flour in my whiskers again. Occupational dusting. Anyone want a roll?

speaker: (narration)
before: Someone has thrown a boot in it. The water has gone politely round the boot.
after: You find a boot in the spring. Clear water slips around its heel. Even here, something finds a way through.

speaker: (narration)
before: Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt'. Twice.
after: You recall the first words of every Gourmand recipe: first, water. Someone has added 'and salt' here. Twice.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.
after: A well with opinions. I'll take a bottle's worth.

speaker: (UI)
before:
Whatever answers duels with all four Paths at once. It is a hard fight.

Lose, and nothing is lost: the well will wait.
after: The Echo duels with all four Paths at once. It is a hard fight. Lose, and nothing is lost: the well will wait.

speaker: (tip)
before: You may play one Infrastructure per turn. Choose wisely, or at least choose.
after: You may play one Infrastructure per turn. Even a bold strategy needs somewhere to plug in.

speaker: (tip)
before: In the main campaign a deck may use two Paths. A multi-Path card counts as both of its Paths.
after: Start with one Path; free your first zone to use two. Multi-Path cards count as both Paths. All Paths may mix after Primm falls.

speaker: (tip)
before: Hover a card to zoom it. Everything the card does is written on it, even the parts that hurt.
after: Hover a card to zoom it. Read the effects; the tiny words can cause enormous problems.

speaker: (tip)
before: Zone HP does not come back after battles inside a zone. Mind it, and mind your snacks.
after: Zone HP does not return after battles inside a zone. Plan your healing stops. Heroism travels poorly on an empty stomach.

speaker: (tip)
before: Your hand holds ten cards at most. Past that, the extras are tossed, and nobody gets a refund.
after: Your hand holds at most ten cards. Extras are tossed. Hoarding has a surprisingly strict ceiling.

speaker: (tip)
before: You get one free mulligan. Use it when the hand is mostly tools and regret.
after: You get one free mulligan. A second opinion on that opening hand, at a very reasonable price.

speaker: (tip)
before: Hustle: this unit can attack the turn it enters. No summoning sickness, no sympathy.
after: Hustle: this unit can attack the turn it enters. Some introductions are brief.

speaker: (tip)
before: Swat: can block Flying units. It is called "swatting" for a reason.
after: Swat: can block Flying units. A grounded response to lofty ambitions.

speaker: (tip)
before: Unbreakable: cannot be destroyed by damage or destroy effects. It can still be shredded, sent back, or sat on.
after: Unbreakable: cannot be destroyed by damage or destroy effects. It can still be shredded or sent back. Read the fine print.

speaker: (tip)
before: Toxic: any damage from this unit destroys what it hits. Hospitality is not its thing.
after: Toxic: any damage from this unit destroys what it hits. Small numbers, serious consequences.

speaker: (tip)
before: Wallflower: cannot attack. It supports you emotionally and sometimes mechanically.
after: Wallflower: cannot attack. Some units make their point by staying exactly where they are.

speaker: (tip)
before: The Beefcake Path has no rest days. This is not a rule, it is a lifestyle.
after: Beefcakes know the value of a rest. Grandmaster Flex would like you to stop calling it a weakness.

speaker: (tip)
before: The Necrocrats file everything in triplicate, including their own funerals.
after: Necrocrats file everything in triplicate. Even the afterlife has a paper trail.

speaker: (tip)
before: The Refusemancers will tell you one thing: nothing is trash if you squint.
after: Refusemancers turn garbage into fertilizer and fertilizer into dinner. Please observe the order.

speaker: (tip)
before: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant, would like you to know that beets are also a weapon.
after: Bertram Beetsworth is Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The promotion is small. His correction will not be.

speaker: (tip)
before: Tilly Tonic tests every potion on herself. Her hair changes color daily. The scorch marks do not.
after: Tilly Tonic tests every potion herself. Her skin changes colour; her enthusiasm remains dangerously consistent.

speaker: (tip)
before: The Endless Buffet has never once been closed for a private event. It is the private event.
after: The Endless Buffet takes food seriously. The food occasionally returns the favour.

speaker: (tip)
before: HP carries over between a dungeon's encounters, and you are fully healed on entering. Plan your fights, not your fears.
after: HP carries between dungeon encounters. Check the dungeon's entry and healing rules; a doorway is not a promise of full health.

speaker: (tip)
before: Talk to everyone in Crosspath. Some of them even have something useful to say.
after: Talk to everyone in Crosspath. Directions, rumours, hats: someone has what you need. Pip has decided it is hats.

speaker: (tip)
before: The Capital is perfectly clean. If you notice a crack, that was not on the brochure.
after: The Capital is perfectly clean. Any crack you notice is a problem with your inspection.

speaker: (tip)
before: Chests sometimes hold more than they let on: a piece of gear, or a pack. Open them all. Treasure is a lifestyle.
after: Chests may hold gear or packs as well as other treasure. Be thorough. It is very respectable nosiness.

speaker: (tip)
before: Zone shops have a Gear stall now. The good stuff appears once you free the zone. Retail therapy, but heroic.
after: Zone shops have a Gear stall. Free the zone to see the good stock. Liberation looks good on you.

speaker: (tip)
before: The checkpoint permit has a box for "reason for living". Most applicants leave it blank.
after: The checkpoint permit has a box for "reason for living". Most applicants leave it blank. The form offers very little room.

speaker: (tip)
before: The great pantry door has a keyhole the size of a dinner plate. The key is the size of a ladle. The math checks out.
after: The pantry keyhole is dinner-plate sized. The key is ladle-sized. Fennel has strong opinions on table settings.

speaker: (tip)
before: Everything is perfect in the Capital. Please report any imperfections to your nearest Perfectly Happy Citizen.
after: Everything is perfect in the Capital. If you disagree, please enjoy the feeling quietly.
